3R replication script (analysis.R)

How to replicate: save the block below as analysis.R, place cleaned.csv (in the export bundle) beside it, then run Rscript analysis.R. The script prints every table shown in the app; the app's numbers were verified byte-for-byte against native R output. Package citations are in section 6.
# Reproducible analysis script generated by Telos
# Run from the folder holding cleaned.csv. Uncomment install.packages() the first time.
# install.packages(c("modelsummary", "rstatix", "ggplot2"))
library(modelsummary)
library(rstatix)
library(ggplot2)
d <- read.csv("cleaned.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
d[["teaching_method"]] <- factor(d[["teaching_method"]])

# === 01 · Welch's ANOVA ===
wdf <- data.frame(y = d[["exam_score"]], g = factor(d[["teaching_method"]]))
print(datasummary_balance(~g, data = wdf, dinm = FALSE))  # Table 1 (Arel-Bundock datasummary)
res <- oneway.test(d[["exam_score"]] ~ factor(d[["teaching_method"]]), var.equal = FALSE)
print(res)
print(rstatix::games_howell_test(data.frame(y = d[["exam_score"]], g = factor(d[["teaching_method"]])), y ~ g))
gf <- factor(d[["teaching_method"]]); agg <- data.frame(g = levels(gf), m = as.numeric(tapply(d[["exam_score"]], gf, mean)))
nn <- as.numeric(tapply(d[["exam_score"]], gf, length)); sdv <- as.numeric(tapply(d[["exam_score"]], gf, sd))
se <- sdv / sqrt(nn); tq <- qt(0.975, nn - 1); agg$lo <- agg$m - tq * se; agg$hi <- agg$m + tq * se
print(ggplot(agg, aes(g, m)) + geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), colour = "#0c447c") + labs(x = NULL, y = NULL))

\includegraphics{figures/01_welch-anova/figure_means-plot.png}

A one-way ANOVA that relaxes the equal-variance assumption but still assumes roughly normal data within each group. A significant F means at least one group mean differs from the others; the Games-Howell post-hoc (also variance-robust) then shows which specific pairs differ. Your significance threshold ($\alpha$) is 0.05.

Welch's ANOVA gave F(2,157.49)=42.31, p $<$ .001, $\omega$\textsuperscript{2}=.34 [.24, 1.00].

Statistical basis: Welch's ANOVA (heteroscedasticity-robust F, fractional df) (Welch, B. L. (1951). "On the comparison of several mean values: an alternative approach." Biometrika, 38(3-4), 330-336.); Games-Howell post-hoc comparisons (also variance-robust) (Kassambara A (2023). rstatix: Pipe-Friendly Framework for Basic Statistical Tests. R package.); $\omega$\textsuperscript{2} effect size (F-to-omega\textsuperscript{2} conversion, no fitted aov model needed) (Ben-Shachar MS, Lüdecke D, Makowski D (2020). "effectsize: Estimation of Effect Size Indices and Standardized Parameters." Journal of Open Source Software, 5(56), 2815.).

\end{document}

Statistical basis (why each test was recommended, and its methodological references)
========================================================================================

Welch's ANOVA
  Why this test: Recommended when you compare three or more group means without assuming equal variances.
    Welch, B. L. (1951). "On the comparison of several mean values: an alternative approach." Biometrika, 38(3-4), 330-336. https://doi.org/10.1093/biomet/38.3-4.330
  Statistical basis:
    Welch's ANOVA (heteroscedasticity-robust F, fractional df)
      Welch, B. L. (1951). "On the comparison of several mean values: an alternative approach." Biometrika, 38(3-4), 330-336. https://doi.org/10.1093/biomet/38.3-4.330
    Games-Howell post-hoc comparisons (also variance-robust)
      Kassambara A (2023). rstatix: Pipe-Friendly Framework for Basic Statistical Tests. R package. https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=rstatix
    ω² effect size (F-to-omega² conversion, no fitted aov model needed)
      Ben-Shachar MS, Lüdecke D, Makowski D (2020). "effectsize: Estimation of Effect Size Indices and Standardized Parameters." Journal of Open Source Software, 5(56), 2815. https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=effectsize

# 12 · Welch's ANOVA

**Question:** 3+ groups, unequal variances

**Scenario:** Campus study: teaching-method effect on exam score, unequal variances (Games-Howell post-hoc).

## Input configuration

- **Dataset:** `campus-study.csv`
- **Configure-data:** app defaults (auto-detected types/levels)
- **Options:** Games-Howell post-hoc; α 0.05

**Role assignments** (drag column → slot):

| Column | Role slot |
|---|---|
| `exam_score` | outcome |
| `teaching_method` | factor |
